questions.answer: Very easy

questions.answer: I didn't need that much help but the exchange office could answer questions about exams etc

Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Not so easy. I was subject to a scam but I had contacts in Barcelona that I lived with until I found something else

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: very good experience. Great city to live in. Just be sure you look for apartments early

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They only accepted me 2 months before the semester started and the subjects available were reviled very late as well but they are good at answering emails if you need help

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It's done only and fairly easy

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Help through emails. They can help with more or less everything

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: very. I got into all my classes

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do it ASAP

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level is not too hard if you just put in a bit of effort. Mine weren't maths based just theory basically

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It's basically like "holdundervisning" where the professor explains the content.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Environmental Economics
Economic Policy
Spanish Economy
Business Economics I
Entrepreneurship

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Well it depends on what they find interesting..

But I liked entrepreneurship because of the professor. He was an economist that focused on how the level of entrepreneurship influenced the economy and as an economist myself I found that interesting

Spanish Economy was nice because I learned about how the spanish economy was influenced by many internal and external factors that weren't always easy to manage from the government's POV. It also gave me an understanding of why southern countries were lacking behind the nordic countries

Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything. They have Erasmus organizations that plan so many things for students

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Depends on their interest. I liked the football opportunities with the app celebreak

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Tibidabo, montserrat hike or just walk around and see the city. You can walk from the beach to la sagrada in less than 30 min so in a weekend you can see everything basically if you don't sit in bar all day

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: just talk to them. They are nice. I got a lot of friends both exchange students and locals

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: late meals

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the hospitality and their life quality

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
have everything in order regarding the application and enrollment. 

Get a lot of friends and don't be shy. Without friends you won't enjoy it as much

Enjoy and have fun

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: They didn't have intro days so I wrote my confirmed days wrong which means my Erasmus grant was calculated wrong

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I got a lot of friends, I became more cultural because I got to know students from all over the world. I learned to speak a bit more spanish and strengthened my English as well

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: nothing

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
